title: Applications of machine learning methods in traffic crash severity modelling: current status and future directions
summary: Review of machine learning in crash severity modelling: imbalanced data remains a major issue, under- and over-sampling are often used despite their limitations, very few studies consider the accuracy and reliability of evaluation metrics, and causality and transferability are listed among the open issues.

title: Investigating two-wheelers risk factors for severe crashes using an interpretable machine learning approach and SHAP analysis
summary: Applies XGBoost with SHAP to French two-wheeler crash data for 2014-2017; department, road category, urbanisation level, two-wheeler category and user age are the most influential features, and severe injury is more likely in rural areas, for older riders and for riders not wearing helmets.

title: Exploring e-scooter risk factors based on interpretable machine learning framework
summary: Analyses 2,400 e-scooter crash records from the UK STATS19 database with machine-learning models; LightGBM performed best and SHAP identified number of vehicles involved, first point of impact, rider gender, lighting, pedestrian crossings and road type as key factors.

title: Cyclist crash severity modeling: A hybrid approach of XGBoost-SHAP and random parameters logit with heterogeneity in means and variances
summary: Combines XGBoost-SHAP with a random parameters logit model with heterogeneity in means and variances to study cyclist crash severity in Great Britain, 2016-2019; XGBoost-SHAP is used to reduce dimensionality and to examine interactions.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Cyclist Injury Severity in Bicycle–Vehicle Crashes in Poland: Association Patterns and Implications for Sustainable Road Safety
summary: Models five ordered injury-severity classes for 152,567 cyclist-involved police records in Poland (2015-2024) with CatBoost, including calendar-based walk-forward stress tests and SHAP; discrimination is modest (hold-out quadratic weighted kappa about 0.20) and the SHAP results are presented as association patterns to be interpreted cautiously.

title: Predicting Child-Bicyclist Crash Severity Under Severe Class Imbalance: A Benchmark of XGBoost and Tabular Deep Learning
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
summary: Benchmarks XGBoost and three tabular deep-learning models on 2,394 Texas child-bicyclist crashes (2017-2022), partitioning the data before feature selection, preprocessing and imbalance treatment; multinomial logistic regression exceeded the primary models on balanced accuracy and macro ROC-AUC, and SHAP rankings showed limited stability relative to cross-seed permutation importance.

title: Decision Curve Analysis: A Novel Method for Evaluating Prediction Models
summary: Introduces decision curve analysis, which evaluates prediction models by net benefit across threshold probabilities and requires only the data set on which the models are tested.

authors.literal: On behalf of Topic Group ‘Evaluating diagnostic tests and prediction models’ of the STRATOS initiative

title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
summary: Argues that calibration of risk prediction models receives too little attention although poorly calibrated algorithms can be misleading and harmful for decision-making, and summarises how to avoid poor calibration at development and assess it at validation.

title: The harm of class imbalance corrections for risk prediction models: illustration and simulation using logistic regression
container: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
summary: Simulation and case study showing that random undersampling, random oversampling and SMOTE give poorly calibrated logistic regression models (minority-class probability strongly overestimated) without a higher area under the ROC curve; a similar sensitivity-specificity balance is obtained by shifting the probability threshold.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
summary: Surveys ML-based science and finds data leakage in 17 fields, collectively affecting 294 papers; gives a taxonomy of eight types of leakage and proposes model info sheets; in a reproducibility study of civil war prediction, complex ML models do not perform substantively better than logistic regression once the errors are corrected.

title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
summary: TRIPOD+AI: harmonised reporting guidance (27-item checklist) for studies developing or evaluating prediction models with regression or machine learning; supersedes the TRIPOD 2015 checklist.

title: Applying oversampling before cross-validation will lead to high bias in radiomics
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
summary: Across 15 radiomic datasets, applying oversampling to all data before cross-validation instead of within the folds produced a large positive bias (up to 0.34 in AUC).

title: Calibrated and Explainable Gradient Boosting for Road Traffic Crash Severity Prediction: SHAP Audit and Cross-Jurisdiction Transfer Evaluation
summary: Crash-severity framework on US-Accidents and UK STATS19 using strict temporal splits throughout; post hoc isotonic calibration strongly reduces expected calibration error, a SHAP audit confirms deletion faithfulness, but explanation stability fails at realistic perturbation levels.

title: Leakage-aware explainable machine learning for highway–rail grade crossing safety screening
summary: Leakage-aware explainable XGBoost screening model for US highway-rail grade crossings; identifies a missingness-driven leakage pathway (absence of weather data becoming predictive of the non-accident class) and addresses it, and reports SHAP attributions with geographic hold-out and feature-ablation checks.

title: Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python
summary: Describes scikit-learn, a Python module integrating a wide range of machine learning algorithms for medium-scale supervised and unsupervised problems.

title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
container: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Introduces LightGBM, a gradient boosting decision tree implementation that uses Gradient-based One-Side Sampling and Exclusive Feature Bundling to improve efficiency and scalability.

title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
container: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Presents SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), a unified framework that assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction and identifies the unique solution with a set of desirable properties within the class of additive feature importance measures.

title: From local explanations to global understanding with explainable AI for trees
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
summary: Presents a polynomial-time algorithm for computing optimal game-theoretic (Shapley value) explanations for tree-based models, a measure of local interaction effects, and tools that combine many local explanations to describe global model structure.

title: True to the Model or True to the Data?
summary: Argues that the choice between interventional and observational conditional expectations in Shapley-value feature attribution is application dependent and comes down to being true to the model or true to the data.

title: Causal Shapley Values: Exploiting Causal Knowledge to Explain Individual Predictions of Complex Models
container: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Proposes causal Shapley values derived with Pearl's do-calculus for general causal graphs, which separate the contributions of direct and indirect effects.

title: Feature relevance quantification in explainable AI: A causal problem
container: Proceedings of the Twenty Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research)
summary: Argues, using Pearl's distinction between observational and interventional conditional probabilities, that unconditional rather than conditional expectations give the right notion of dropping features when quantifying feature relevance with Shapley values.

title: Problems with Shapley-value-based explanations as feature importance measures
container: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research)
summary: Shows that mathematical problems arise when Shapley values are used for feature importance, that the mitigations introduce further complexity such as the need for causal reasoning, and argues that Shapley values do not suit human-centric goals of explainability.

title: Predictive and Causal Implications of using Shapley Value for Model Interpretation
container: Proceedings of the 2020 KDD Workshop on Causal Discovery (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research)
summary: Analyses the Shapley value in a Bayesian network framework and concludes that a variable's Shapley value does not reflect its causal relationship with the target and that Shapley-based feature selection is not predictively optimal in general.

title: Causal Interpretations of Black-Box Models
summary: Notes that the partial dependence plot has the same formula as the back-door adjustment and sets out three requirements for causal interpretation of black-box models: good predictive performance, domain knowledge in the form of a causal diagram, and suitable visualisation tools.

title: General Pitfalls of Model-Agnostic Interpretation Methods for Machine Learning Models
container: xxAI - Beyond Explainable AI (Lecture Notes in Computer Science)
summary: Catalogues general pitfalls of model-agnostic interpretation methods (partial dependence, permutation importance, Shapley values), including interpreting models that do not generalise, ignoring feature dependence and uncertainty, and making unjustified causal interpretations.

title: Empirical Comparison of Causal Machine Learning and Post-Hoc AI Interpretability Models for Risk Factor Analysis: An Application to Medical Specialty Choice
container: Opening the Personal Gate between Technology and Health Care (Studies in Health Technology and Informatics)
summary: In a cohort of 399 medical students, effects estimated with DoubleML were contrasted with SHAP explanations from an earlier predictive model: SHAP directions generally matched DoubleML for strong, well-separated factors but diverged for weaker or correlated ones.

title: Estimation of Regression Coefficients When Some Regressors are not Always Observed
container: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Proposes a class of semiparametric estimators based on inverse probability weighted estimating equations for regression when some regressors are missing at random, and derives the efficient estimator in that class.

title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
container: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
summary: Introduces the false discovery rate, the expected proportion of falsely rejected hypotheses, and a simple sequential Bonferroni-type procedure that controls it for independent test statistics.

title: Dealing with limited overlap in estimation of average treatment effects
summary: Develops a systematic approach to limited overlap in estimating average treatment effects and shows that discarding units with estimated propensity scores outside [0.1, 0.9] is a good approximation to the optimal rule.

title: A Practitioner’s Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
summary: Practitioner's guide to cluster-robust inference: when errors are correlated within clusters default standard errors can greatly overstate precision; covers few clusters, multi-way clustering and estimators other than OLS.

title: Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters
summary: Introduces double/debiased machine learning: Neyman-orthogonal scores combined with cross-fitting remove the regularisation and overfitting bias of plug-in ML nuisance estimates, giving approximately unbiased, normally distributed estimators of low-dimensional causal parameters.

title: Making Sense of Sensitivity: Extending Omitted Variable Bias
container: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
summary: Extends the omitted variable bias framework for sensitivity analysis, introducing the robustness value and the partial R2 of the treatment with the outcome, and a formal procedure to bound confounder strength by benchmarking against observed covariates.

title: Debiased machine learning of conditional average treatment effects and other causal functions
summary: Provides estimation and inference for the best linear predictor of structural functions such as conditional average treatment effects using a Neyman-orthogonal signal; when the basis functions are group indicators the estimand is the group average treatment effect.

title: DoubleML - An Object-Oriented Implementation of Double Machine Learning in Python
summary: Describes DoubleML, an open-source Python library implementing the double machine learning framework of Chernozhukov et al. (2018) for a variety of causal models, with valid inference when nuisance parameters are estimated by machine learning.

title: DoubleML: An Object-Oriented Implementation of Double Machine Learning in R
summary: Introduces the R package DoubleML and the double machine learning framework (Neyman orthogonality, machine learning estimation of nuisance components, sample splitting), covering partially linear and interactive regression models.

title: Fisher–Schultz Lecture: Generic Machine Learning Inference on Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in Randomized Experiments, With an Application to Immunization in India
summary: Proposes generic machine-learning inference on features of heterogeneous effects in randomized experiments (best linear predictors, sorted group average effects, characteristics of most and least affected units), using repeated data splitting and quantile aggregation.

title: Long Story Short: Omitted Variable Bias in Causal Machine Learning
summary: Develops a general theory of omitted variable bias for causal parameters estimated with machine learning, showing that plausibility judgments on the maximum explanatory power of omitted variables are sufficient to bound the bias, with accompanying inference methods.

title: The statistical analysis of highway crash-injury severities: A review and assessment of methodological alternatives
summary: Summarises the evolution of research and current thinking on the statistical analysis of motor-vehicle crash-injury severities and discusses future methodological directions.

title: Unobserved heterogeneity and the statistical analysis of highway accident data
summary: Addresses unobserved heterogeneity in the statistical analysis of highway accident data.

title: Temporal instability and the analysis of highway accident data
summary: Addresses temporal instability in the analysis of highway accident data.

title: Big data, traditional data and the tradeoffs between prediction and causality in highway-safety analysis
summary: Discusses the trade-off between predictive capability and the ability to uncover causality across traditional, advanced statistical and data-driven methods in highway safety, noting that data from observed crashes can over-represent inherently riskier individuals.

title: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects in road safety analysis using generalized random forests
summary: Introduces generalized random forests for heterogeneous treatment effects in road safety, compares them in simulations with outcome regression, propensity score and doubly robust methods, and applies them to the UK speed camera programme.

title: Causal inference for transport research
container: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
summary: Consolidated overview of causal inference for transport research based on potential outcomes, with core estimation methods, case-study simulations and R code.

title: Mandatory speed limits and crash frequency on motorways — A causal machine learning approach
container: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
summary: Applies a causal forest to estimate the effects of mandatory speed limits on injury crash frequencies on German motorway segments and examines bias from spatial overfitting.

title: Exploring the causal effects of hazardous driving behaviors on pedestrian-vehicle crash injury severity based on causal machine learning
container: International Journal of Injury Control and Safety Promotion
summary: Uses causal machine learning together with SHAP and a causal tree to study the effects of hazardous driving behaviours on pedestrian injury severity in pedestrian-vehicle crashes, reporting heterogeneous conditional average treatment effects.

title: A Systematic Review of Causal Machine Learning Approaches in Road Crash Analysis
container: Proceedings of IndabaX Nigeria 2026: Building Scalable AI That Works: From Research to Deployment in Resource-Constrained Environments (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research)
summary: PRISMA review of 35 articles (2021-2025) classified as predictive, interpretable or causal ML; most remain predictive ensembles or explainability tools such as SHAP, and the gaps named include the continued conflation of predictive feature importance with causal effect and the absence of standardised causal benchmarks.

title: A Structural Approach to Selection Bias
summary: Argues that the various forms of selection bias share one causal structure: conditioning on a common effect of two variables, one related to exposure and the other to the outcome.

title: Underreporting in traffic accident data, bias in parameters and the structure of injury severity models
summary: Treats traffic accident data as outcome-based samples in which higher severities are over-represented because of underreporting, and shows that this biases parameters of injury severity models, including the effect of safety belt use.

title: The preregistration revolution
container: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Makes the case for preregistration (defining research questions and the analysis plan before observing outcomes) to separate prediction from postdiction, and discusses strategies for cases such as preexisting data.

title: A Crash Course in Good and Bad Controls
summary: Describes graphical tools, through illustrative examples, for deciding when adding a variable to a regression helps or harms the causal interpretation of a coefficient (the 'bad control' problem).

title: A note on observed injury bias in police-reported pre-crash travel speed estimates
summary: A note on observed injury bias in police-reported pre-crash travel speed estimates.
